Our expected burden from alternative regulation remains 12. Under the alternative-regulation assessment, continued support yields 12 minus the common proposal cost of 6, for a payoff of 6. The coalition therefore continues to support the federal proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Across comparable cases, internal records should show that support responds to revised estimates of alternative-regulation burdens, while revisions limited to competitive benefits do not systematically change support.","derivation":"Under SA, support depends jointly on the expected alternative-regulation burden, the common proposal cost, and the probabilistic decision rule. Competitive-benefit revisions do not enter the SA payoff.","extra_assumption":"Researchers can reliably date and distinguish internal revisions to alternative-regulation burdens from revisions to competitive benefits."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_04_02","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The reliable notice lowered the expected burden of alternative carbon regulation from 12 to 2, while the incremental competitive benefit remains 12. Continued support now yields 2 minus the proposal cost of 6, or −4. The coalition has therefore ended its support.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition no longer supports the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Withdrawals should be preceded by internal reassessments emphasizing diminished exposure to alternative regulation more often than by reassessments confined to competitive conditions.","derivation":"SA makes the alternative-regulation burden decisive after subtracting the proposal cost; the notice structure changes only one benefit, and the decision rule usually follows the resulting payoff sign.","extra_assumption":"Document archives preserve assessments made before the corresponding public position changes."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_04_03","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The notice reduced the incremental competitive benefit from 12 to 2 but left the expected alternative-regulation burden at 12. The SA calculation remains 12 minus 6, producing a positive payoff of 6. Despite that assessment, the coalition decided to discontinue support.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition has discontinued its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"A small minority of internal records should document position choices that conflict with the sign of the contemporaneous SA payoff, without requiring a change in the underlying burden estimate.","derivation":"The SA payoff rule and the independent 0.05 decision reversal probability jointly imply occasional departures from the payoff-prescribed position.","extra_assumption":"Internal documents preserve both the contemporaneous payoff inputs and the final decision."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_04_04","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The private notice lowered the incremental competitive benefit to 2. The expected burden of alternative regulation remains 12. Because the SA payoff is 12 less the proposal cost of 6, continued support retains a payoff of 6. The coalition will maintain its endorsement.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition maintains its endorsement of the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Internal commercial assessments may deteriorate without producing a corresponding public retreat when expected exposure to alternative regulation remains above the proposal cost.","derivation":"This follows jointly from SA excluding competitive benefit from its payoff, the proposal cost of 6, and the rule linking a nonnegative payoff to support subject to rare reversal.","extra_assumption":"Researchers can link commercial assessments and public-position records to the same decision episode."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_04_05","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The notice reduced the expected burden from alternative carbon regulation to 2, leaving the incremental competitive benefit at 12. Subtracting the proposal cost of 6 gives an SA payoff of −4. The coalition accordingly decided not to support the proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Occasional public statements should contradict contemporaneous internal decision records even when the internal SA calculation clearly favors one position.","derivation":"The faithful internal memo and the independent 0.05 public communication error jointly imply rare documentary contradictions between internal and public records.","extra_assumption":"Researchers can establish that the internal and public documents refer to the same proposal and decision date."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_04_06","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The reliable notice revised the expected burden of alternative regulation from 12 to 2. The competitive benefit remains 12, but it does not determine the SA payoff. With the proposal cost fixed at 6, continued support yields −4. The coalition has withdrawn its endorsement.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition has withdrawn its endorsement of the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Where internal documents separate regulatory exposure from competitive gains, changes in the former should predict position changes more strongly under SA.","derivation":"SA uses the alternative-regulation burden minus the common proposal cost, whereas the competitive benefit is excluded; the probabilistic decision rule weakens but does not eliminate this association.","extra_assumption":"A sufficiently large collection of comparable, accurately classified documents is available."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_04_07","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The notice lowered the incremental competitive benefit from 12 to 2 while leaving the expected alternative-regulation burden at 12. Continued support therefore has an SA payoff of 12 minus 6, equal to 6. The coalition remains supportive.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition remains supportive of the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Documents discussing reduced competitive gains should often coexist with unchanged endorsements when they also indicate that alternative-regulation exposure remains substantial.","derivation":"The notice can reduce competitive benefit alone, but SA bases the decision on alternative-regulation burden net of the proposal cost; the usual decision therefore remains support.","extra_assumption":"Internal documents report both the type of revised expectation and the timing of endorsements."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_04_08","memo":"SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The private notice reduced the estimated incremental competitive benefit to 2. Expected exposure to alternative carbon regulation remains 12. Applying SA, the payoff from support is 12 minus the proposal cost of 6, leaving 6. The coalition will continue supporting the proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition will continue supporting the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Researchers should find greater continuity in endorsements following competitive-benefit revisions than following equally sized downward revisions in expected alternative-regulation burdens.","derivation":"The two notice types are equally likely and equally sized, but only the alternative-regulation burden enters the SA payoff; the shared decision-error rate leaves a systematic difference between documentary sequences.","extra_assumption":"The documentary sample does not select cases according to whether support continued or ended."}]}
